title: Prakrama 3, Sarga 7. Beholding Sri Viraja
html:
Mukunda vouches that the toll-collectors are harmless, but at the barrier he is bound and held until evening; the chief of the toll-collectors comes to the Lord to make amends; next morning the Lord goes to Viraja, the sight of whom is equal to the sight of Bhagavan

Verse 1

ततः प्रणम्य तं भक्त्या मुकुन्दोऽम्बष्ठ ईश्वरम्।
प्राह प्रफुल्लवदनः सहर्षं जगदीश्वरम्॥१॥

tataḥ praṇamya taṁ bhaktyā mukundo'mbaṣṭha īśvaram|
prāha praphullavadanaḥ saharṣaṁ jagadīśvaram||1||

tatah — then; pranamya — bowing; tam — to Him; bhaktya — with devotion; mukundah — Mukunda; ambashthah — the Ambashtha (vaidya); ishvaram — to the Lord; praha — said; praphulla-vadanah — with a beaming face; sa-harsham — joyfully; jagat-ishvaram — to the Lord of the world.

1Then Mukunda the vaidya1 bowed with devotion to the Lord and, his face beaming, joyfully said to the Lord of the world:

Verse 2

भगवन्नत्र नास्ते वै दानिनो भयमण्वपि।
जानामि सर्वतो लोकान्ये वसन्त्यत्र दुर्मदान्॥२॥

bhagavannatra nāste vai dānino bhayamaṇvapi|
jānāmi sarvato lokānye vasantyatra durmadān||2||

bhagavan — O Bhagavan; atra — here; na aste — there is not; vai — indeed; daninah — from the toll-collector; bhayam — danger; anu — the least; api — even; janami — I know; sarvatah — through and through; lokan — the people; ye — who; vasanti — live; atra — here; durmadan — arrogant.

2"Bhagavan, here there is not the least danger from the toll-collectors: I know the people who live here through and through, arrogant as they may be."

Verse 3

तच्छ्रुत्वा भगवान्प्राह स्मितकान्तनवाननः।
एतावद्भयमस्माकं पालनं भवता कृतम्॥३॥

tacchrutvā bhagavānprāha smitakāntanavānanaḥ|
etāvadbhayamasmākaṁ pālanaṁ bhavatā kṛtam||3||

tat — that; shrutva — hearing; bhagavan — Bhagavan; praha — said; smita-kanta-nava-ananah — His youthful face lovely with a smile; etavat — so much (and no more); bhayam — danger; asmakam — for us; palanam — protection; bhavata — by you; kritam — has been provided.

3Hearing this, Bhagavan, His youthful face lovely with a smile, said, "So that is all there is to our danger: you have already seen to our protection."

Verse 4

इत्युक्त्वा प्रययौ भिक्षां कर्तुं लोकेषु शिक्षया।
लक्ष्मीकान्तः स्वयं कृष्णो न्यासिवंशधरो हरिः॥४॥

ityuktvā prayayau bhikṣāṁ kartuṁ lokeṣu śikṣayā|
lakṣmīkāntaḥ svayaṁ kṛṣṇo nyāsivaṁśadharo hariḥ||4||

iti — thus; uktva — having spoken; prayayau — set out; bhiksham — alms; kartum — to gather; lokeshu — among people; shikshaya — to teach by example; lakshmi-kantah — the beloved of Lakshmi; svayam — Himself; krishnah — Krishna; nyasi-vamsha-dharah — bearing the bamboo staff of a sannyasi; harih — Hari.

4So saying, Hari — Krishna Himself, the beloved of Lakshmi, now bearing the bamboo staff of a sannyasi — set out to beg alms, to teach people by His own example.

Verse 5

नित्यानन्दावधूतश्च सर्वशक्तिसमन्वितः।
श्रीमद्गदाधरो विप्रो मुकुन्दाद्याश्च सज्जनाः॥५॥

nityānandāvadhūtaśca sarvaśaktisamanvitaḥ|
śrīmadgadādharo vipro mukundādyāśca sajjanāḥ||5||

nityananda-avadhutah — Nityananda the Avadhuta; cha — and; sarva-shakti-samanvitah — endowed with every power; shrimat-gadadharah — the glorious Gadadhara; viprah — the brahmana; mukunda-adyah — Mukunda and others; cha — and; sat-janah — virtuous men.

5Nityananda the Avadhuta, endowed with every power, the glorious Gadadhara, the brahmana, Mukunda and the other virtuous companions also went out to gather alms.

Verse 6

जग्मुर्भिक्षाटनेनात्र दानी तानप्यवर्जयत्।
बद्ध्वा मुकुन्दं संरक्ष्य दिनमेवानयत्क्रुधा॥६॥

jagmurbhikṣāṭanenātra dānī tānapyavarjayat|
baddhvā mukundaṁ saṁrakṣya dinamevānayatkrudhā||6||

jagmuh — went; bhiksha-atanena — on their round for alms; atra — here; dani — the toll-collector; tan — them; api — too; avarjayat — barred; baddhva — binding; mukundam — Mukunda; samrakshya — keeping under guard; dinam — the day; eva — whole; anayat — kept (him); krudha — in anger.

6But here the toll-collector barred their way too: in his anger he bound Mukunda and kept him under guard the whole day.

Verse 7

ततः सायाह्नवेलायां गृहीत्वा कम्बलोत्तमम्।
मोचयामास तान्सर्वांस्ततो विमनसो ययुः॥७॥

tataḥ sāyāhnavelāyāṁ gṛhītvā kambalottamam|
mocayāmāsa tānsarvāṁstato vimanaso yayuḥ||7||

tatah — then; sayahna-velayam — at the hour of evening; grihitva — taking; kambala-uttamam — the finest blanket; mochayam asa — released; tan — them; sarvan — all; tatah — then; vimanasah — downcast; yayuh — went away.

7Only at the hour of evening, after taking the finest blanket, did he release them all, and they went away downcast.

Verse 8

ते गत्वा ब्राह्मणान्भिक्षां कृत्वा बुभुजिरे ततः।
नित्यानन्दो महातेजाः केन लक्ष्यः स्वयं प्रभुः॥८॥

te gatvā brāhmaṇānbhikṣāṁ kṛtvā bubhujire tataḥ|
nityānando mahātejāḥ kena lakṣyaḥ svayaṁ prabhuḥ||8||

te — they; gatva — going; brahmanan — to brahmanas; bhiksham — alms; kritva — receiving; bubhujire — ate; tatah — then; nityanandah — Nityananda; maha-tejah — of great might; kena — by whom; lakshyah — could be traced; svayam — Himself; prabhuh — the Lord.

8They went to some brahmanas, received alms and ate. But Nityananda, full of great might — the Lord Himself — who could keep track of Him2?

Verse 9

ततस्ते मण्डपं जग्मुः शयनार्थं द्विजाश्रमे।
नित्यानन्दो हसन्बद्धं तत्रागत उदारधीः॥९॥

tataste maṇḍapaṁ jagmuḥ śayanārthaṁ dvijāśrame|
nityānando hasanbaddhaṁ tatrāgata udāradhīḥ||9||

tatah — then; te — they; mandapam — to the pavilion; jagmuh — went; shayana-artham — to sleep; dvija-ashrame — at a brahmana's dwelling; nityanandah — Nityananda; hasan — laughing; baddham — at the one who had been bound; tatra — there; agatah — arrived; udara-dhih — the large-hearted.

9Then they went to sleep in a pavilion at a brahmana's dwelling, and there the large-hearted Nityananda arrived, laughing at the one who had been bound.

Verse 10

तत्रैव भगवान्भिक्षां कृत्वा स्वयमुपस्थितः।
तं दृष्ट्वाकथयत्सर्वं दानिभिर्यत्कृतं बलात्॥१०॥

tatraiva bhagavānbhikṣāṁ kṛtvā svayamupasthitaḥ|
taṁ dṛṣṭvākathayatsarvaṁ dānibhiryatkṛtaṁ balāt||10||

tatra — there; eva — likewise; bhagavan — Bhagavan; bhiksham — alms; kritva — having gathered; svayam — Himself; upasthitah — arrived; tam — Him; drishtva — seeing; akathayat — told; sarvam — all; danibhih — by the toll-collectors; yat — what; kritam — was done; balat — by force.

10There too came Bhagavan Himself, having gathered His alms; and on seeing Him they told Him all that the toll-collectors had done by force.

Verse 11

तच्छ्रुत्वा भगवांस्तिष्ठ भद्रं भद्रं भविष्यति।
तदीया शक्ती राजानं प्रेषयामास सत्वरम्॥११॥

tacchrutvā bhagavāṁstiṣṭha bhadraṁ bhadraṁ bhaviṣyati|
tadīyā śaktī rājānaṁ preṣayāmāsa satvaram||11||

tat — that; shrutva — hearing; bhagavan — Bhagavan; tishtha — wait; bhadram — well; bhadram — well; bhavishyati — it will be; tadiya — His; shaktih — power; rajanam — the ruler; preshayam asa — sent; satvaram — at once.

11Hearing this, Bhagavan said, "Wait — all will be well, all will be well." And His power at once sent the ruler there3.

Verse 12

तत्क्षणात्तत्र दानीशः समागत्य पदाम्बुजम्।
हरेर्ववन्द तं प्राहुर्मुकुन्दाद्या महत्तमाः॥१२॥

tatkṣaṇāttatra dānīśaḥ samāgatya padāmbujam|
harervavanda taṁ prāhurmukundādyā mahattamāḥ||12||

tat-kshanat — at that very moment; tatra — there; dani-ishah — the chief of the toll-collectors; samagatya — arriving; pada-ambujam — the lotus feet; hareh — of Hari; vavanda — worshipped; tam — to him; prahuh — told (it); mukunda-adyah — Mukunda and the others; mahattamah — the great souls.

12At that very moment the chief of the toll-collectors arrived and worshipped the lotus feet of Hari, and the great souls headed by Mukunda told him what had happened.

Verse 13

प्राह च तत्कृते सर्वान्दण्डवाटस्थिताञ्जनान्।
प्रहरिष्यामि तान्दुष्टान्न करिष्यन्ति ते यथा॥१३॥

prāha ca tatkṛte sarvāndaṇḍavāṭasthitāñjanān|
prahariṣyāmi tānduṣṭānna kariṣyanti te yathā||13||

praha — said; cha — and; tat-krite — for this; sarvan — all; danda-vata-sthitan — posted at the barrier; janan — the men; praharishyami — I shall have beaten; tan — those; dushtan — wicked; na — not; karishyanti — will do (it again); te — they; yatha — so that.

13And he said, "For this I shall have all the men posted at the barrier beaten, those villains, so that they never do such a thing again."

Verse 14

तद्भृत्यैर्यत्कृतं कर्म तच्छ्रुत्वा दुःखितोऽभवत्।
दानीशः कम्बलं नूत्नं बहुमूल्यं प्रदत्तवान्॥१४॥

tadbhṛtyairyatkṛtaṁ karma tacchrutvā duḥkhito'bhavat|
dānīśaḥ kambalaṁ nūtnaṁ bahumūlyaṁ pradattavān||14||

tat-bhrityaih — by his servants; yat — what; kritam — done; karma — deed; tat — that; shrutva — hearing; duhkhitah — grieved; abhavat — became; dani-ishah — the chief of the toll-collectors; kambalam — a blanket; nutnam — new; bahu-mulyam — costly; pradattavan — gave.

14Hearing what his servants had done, the chief of the toll-collectors was grieved, and he gave them a new and costly blanket.

Verse 15

इत्युक्त्वा प्रणमन्सोऽपि गतः स्वगृहमृद्धिमत्।
सर्वं त्यक्त्वा हरेः पादं चिन्तयामास शुद्धधीः॥१५॥

ityuktvā praṇamanso'pi gataḥ svagṛhamṛddhimat|
sarvaṁ tyaktvā hareḥ pādaṁ cintayāmāsa śuddhadhīḥ||15||

iti — thus; uktva — having spoken; pranaman — bowing down; sah — he; api — too; gatah — went; sva-griham — to his house; riddhimat — wealthy; sarvam — everything; tyaktva — giving up; hareh — of Hari; padam — the foot; chintayam asa — meditated on; shuddha-dhih — with purified mind.

15Having spoken thus, he bowed down and went off to his wealthy house; and from then on, giving up everything, he meditated with a purified mind on the foot of Hari.

Verse 16

एवं तेषां चाभिमानं शमयित्वा निशां सुखम्।
सुप्त्वा निनाय देवेशः प्रातरुत्थाय सत्वरः॥१६॥

evaṁ teṣāṁ cābhimānaṁ śamayitvā niśāṁ sukham|
suptvā nināya deveśaḥ prātarutthāya satvaraḥ||16||

evam — thus; tesham — their; cha — and; abhimanam — wounded pride; shamayitva — having soothed; nisham — the night; sukham — happily; suptva — sleeping; ninaya — spent; deva-ishah — the Lord of the gods; pratah — in the morning; utthaya — rising; satvarah — in haste.

16Having thus soothed their wounded pride, the Lord of the gods slept happily through the night, and in the morning He rose in haste

Verse 17

जगाम विरजां द्रष्टुं सर्वलोकैकपावनीम्।
यां दृष्ट्वा श्रद्धया भक्त्या मुच्यते भवबन्धनात्॥१७॥

jagāma virajāṁ draṣṭuṁ sarvalokaikapāvanīm|
yāṁ dṛṣṭvā śraddhayā bhaktyā mucyate bhavabandhanāt||17||

jagama — went; virajam — Viraja; drashtum — to see; sarva-loka-eka-pavanim — the sole purifier of all the worlds; yam — whom; drishtva — seeing; shraddhaya — with faith; bhaktya — with devotion; muchyate — one is freed; bhava-bandhanat — from the bonds of worldly existence.

17and went to see Viraja4, the sole purifier of all the worlds: whoever beholds her with faith and devotion is freed from the bonds of worldly existence.

Verse 18

भगवद्दर्शने यादृक्फलमाप्नोति मानवः।
तादृक्फलमवाप्नोति विरजामुखदर्शने॥१८॥

bhagavaddarśane yādṛkphalamāpnoti mānavaḥ|
tādṛkphalamavāpnoti virajāmukhadarśane||18||

bhagavat-darshane — on seeing Bhagavan; yadrik — such as; phalam — fruit; apnoti — gains; manavah — a man; tadrik — such; phalam — fruit; avapnoti — he obtains; viraja-mukha-darshane — on seeing the face of Viraja.

18Whatever fruit a man gains by seeing Bhagavan, that same fruit he obtains by seeing the face of Viraja5.

Verse 19

यत्रास्ति भगवान्देवः साक्षाच्छ्रीमत्त्रिलोचनः।
काश्यां वा विरजायां वा मृतिर्मोक्षप्रदायिनी॥१९॥

yatrāsti bhagavāndevaḥ sākṣācchrīmattrilocanaḥ|
kāśyāṁ vā virajāyāṁ vā mṛtirmokṣapradāyinī||19||

yatra — where; asti — dwells; bhagavan — the divine; devah — god; sakshat — in person; shrimat-trilochanah — glorious Trilochana; kashyam — in Kashi; va — or; virajayam — at Viraja; va — or; mritih — death; moksha-pradayini — bestows liberation.

19Both in Kashi and at Viraja, where the divine and glorious Trilochana6 dwells in person, death bestows liberation.

Verse 20

वाराणस्यां मृते यादृक्प्रीतिमाप्नोति शङ्करः।
ततोऽधिकतरा प्रीतिर्विरजायां मृते भवेत्॥२०॥

vārāṇasyāṁ mṛte yādṛkprītimāpnoti śaṅkaraḥ|
tato'dhikatarā prītirvirajāyāṁ mṛte bhavet||20||

varanasyam — in Varanasi; mrite — when (one) dies; yadrik — such as; pritim — joy; apnoti — feels; shankarah — Shankara; tatah — than that; adhika-tara — greater; pritih — joy; virajayam — at Viraja; mrite — when one dies; bhavet — there is.

20Whatever joy Shankara feels when a man dies in Varanasi, still greater is his joy when one dies at Viraja.

Verse 21

तां दृष्ट्वा प्रययौ कृष्णः सर्वलोकैकपावनः।
कृष्णसङ्कीर्तनं कृत्वा भक्तवर्गसमन्वितः॥२१॥

tāṁ dṛṣṭvā prayayau kṛṣṇaḥ sarvalokaikapāvanaḥ|
kṛṣṇasaṅkīrtanaṁ kṛtvā bhaktavargasamanvitaḥ||21||

tam — her; drishtva — having seen; prayayau — went on; krishnah — Krishna; sarva-loka-eka-pavanah — the sole purifier of all the worlds; krishna-sankirtanam — the sankirtana of Krishna's names; kritva — performing; bhakta-varga-samanvitah — with the company of devotees.

21Having beheld her, Krishna, the sole purifier of all the worlds, went on His way, singing the names of Krishna in sankirtana together with the company of His devotees.

Thus ends the seventh sarga, "Beholding Sri Viraja" (Shri-viraja-darshana), of the third prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. Literally "the Ambashtha", the vaidya (physician) caste to which Mukunda Datta belonged.
  2. That is, Nityananda had wandered off on His own and turned up only later (v. 9).
  3. The "ruler" is the chief of the toll-collectors (vv. 12–14). The Lord sends no one for him: it is His power that brings the ruler there.
  4. Viraja is the goddess worshipped at Yajapura (Jajpur); see Sarga 3.06, v. 17.
  5. Such comparisons of fruits are praise of a holy place (mahatmya), common in the Puranas; they do not make the goddess equal to Bhagavan. The Lord Himself, coming to Viraja, only bows to her and asks for loving devotion (3.06, v. 18), as befits a devotee.
  6. Trilochana ("the Three-eyed") is Shiva; his principal linga in Varanasi bears the same name (cf. Sarga 3.06, v. 20).
